symptom: A Netlify deploy could be exact-main when first observed while protected main advanced again during the same terminal verification window.
A hidden fallback error string remained present in deployed HTML/DOM and could be mistaken by text-only diagnostics for a user-visible language-switch failure.
Tool/orchestration timeouts could tempt duplicate deploy attempts even when provider state had already advanced successfully.
root_cause: Terminal proof was sampled across moving authorities instead of rejoining current protected main, current provider commit identity and current-SHA functional evidence at closure time.
Text-source diagnostics and user-visible interaction evidence were not explicitly separated in the terminal truth model.
Execution transport timeout and application/provider failure were not explicitly separated in recovery policy.
prevention: Re-read protected main immediately before terminal closure.
Require Netlify current production state=ready and commit_ref equal to the freshly read main SHA.
Require Production Release Readback and Production Source Snapshot for that same SHA plus the applicable functional/browser verifier.
If main advances follow the same canonical lineage and re-establish current-head proof; never create a competing deployment lineage merely to chase the pointer.
After orchestration or tool timeouts re-read provider truth before retrying; timeout alone is not application failure.

For interaction defects distinguish hidden DOM/source fallback copy from visible browser state. A string match is diagnostic only; visible failure in the canonical browser verifier remains fail-closed.
failed_approaches: Treating an earlier exact-main deploy as terminal after main advanced again.
Treating a hidden DOM fallback string as equivalent to visible runtime failure.
Retrying deployment immediately after orchestration timeout without first re-reading Netlify current state.

evidence.browser_contract: pricing lifecycle + plan group + yearly billing + NL→EN→NL on mandatory public routes
